title: If You Put Vodka in the Freezer, You're Doing it Wrong
description:
Whether you prefer your martini’s shaken or stirred, there’s one way you shouldn’t take the vodka.

From the freezer!

Unless it’s the cheap stuff.

Take it from the creator of premium vodka brand Grey Goose.

He recently told Business Insider that storing vodka in the freezer is a no-no because the low temps overwhelm the flavor within the liquid.

Basically, keeping premium vodka extremely cold will block the more sophisticated flavors and aromas.

The head mixologist for Belvedere told Complex the same thing.

But if you’ve got inexpensive booze, keeping the bottle in the freezer will hide any aggressive, burning notes.

So, you’re probably doing yourself a favor to put the cheap stuff on ice.

Because he’s the creator of Grey Goose, he did some promoting and says the best temperature is 32 to 39 degrees Fahrenheit.

Having said this, the vodka expert says the booze can be too aggressive at room temperature, so add a few ice cubes before you take a sip.

That’s the spirit!
